Subject: Q2 Renewal: usage health & term-flex discussion

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for the time last week. I pulled together Brightline’s usage and performance snapshot for Q1 (attached) and wanted to call out a few items ahead of our renewal conversation:

- Token consumption: 12.4M tokens in Q1, ~48% QoQ growth driven by increased user prompts and a 30% rise in system-generated augmentations.
- Cost: billable token cost ran ~ $2.7k/day on average; projected run-rate without commit is ~ $81k/month.
- Latency: P95 inference latency at current model mix is ~220ms; p99 tails spike during peak ingest windows.
- Efficiency: We see a 9% opportunity from batching + prefix caching for the current traffic shape; quantization would add another ~15% token-cost reduction for non-critical models.

Options I recommend we consider for the renewal:
1) 12-month committed capacity with stepped tranches (10M tokens/month starting month 1, stepping to 20M by month 6) — pricing to reflect committed discount.
2) Dedicated pool pilot (60–90 days) to validate latency and cost lift with auto-failover to hosted service.
3) Short-term burst credit (60 days) to smooth upcoming product launch traffic while finalizing commit terms.

Attached: brightline_q1_usage_Mar2027.csv and a one-page ops snapshot (ops_latency_snapshot_Mar2027.txt).

Would you be available for a 30-min alignment this week to walk the numbers and pick a preferred path? I can share a compact ROI slide that maps committed pricing to estimated cost per 1M tokens and latency improvements.

Next steps if you’re open: 1) confirm a time, 2) tell us which option(s) look most relevant, 3) we’ll prepare a draft term amendment and pilot plan.

Thanks —
Avery

Avery / Monica —

Forwarding Sanjay’s reply. Quick internal thoughts before we jump on the call:

- We can produce the user vs system token split from their logs; should be straightforward from the usage CSV.
- Cost modelling: rough estimate for moving 40% of inference to Dedicated (same model family, A10G equivalent) is ~22–28% unit-cost reduction given predictable batching and local KV cache — depends on model mix and whether they accept FP16/4-bit quantized variants for the recommender.
- p99 improvement: typically dedicated pools reduce tail by 15–35% in our benchmarks for steady-state traffic; during bursts it’s tied to queueing and autoscaling config.

Proposal for the customer:
1) ROI one-pager (Avery to deliver) showing committed vs on-demand and a 45-day dedicated pilot scope limited to Recommendation traffic.
2) Offer: 10% committed discount off list for a 12-month term + 60 days burst credits (to cover launch window).
3) If pilot shows the expected cost delta, include a step-up clause to increase committed capacity at month 3 with pre-agreed pricing tranches.

I’ve penciled in Wed 4/21 10:30 PT (we can nudge to 10:00 if they prefer). Avery — I can join the call and handle the pricing walk; Monica, can you prep a short ops checklist we can share (ingest windows, model variants, SLO targets)?
